history.user: I have finally put my name down for an allotment at the Fenwick Road site. I filled in the form at the parish office and the woman there said the waiting list is long, so I should not hold my breath.
history.assistant: Name on the list, then. That is the part you could do, and you have done it.

history.user: Apparently the committee writes to you by post when a plot comes free. Could be months. I am going to try to forget about it until something drops through the door.
history.assistant: By post, some month or other. Forgetting about it is probably the only sane way to wait.

history.user: I emailed the director of the community choir tonight to ask whether I could audition for the winter concert. Took me three drafts to make it sound casual.
history.assistant: Three drafts to sound casual. It is sent now, which is what counts.

history.user: Nothing back from the choir yet. I have checked my inbox more times today than I would like to admit.
history.assistant: Checking does not hurry it along, and everybody does it anyway.

steps.text: They got back to me at last!
Spent the afternoon turning the compost heap at Mum's. I kept thinking how much I want a patch of ground of my own to dig.
And when I got home there was a letter from the committee on the mat. They have finally answered.
